name: Tarkle
description: Upload, manage and share your business files. Connect Tarkle to your AI assistant to upload, store and organize your team's files and folders, share files, and request documents from your team, clients and partners on your own domain.
author: Tarkle

tools.name: tarkle_list_workspaces
tools.description: List the Tarkle workspaces the signed-in user can reach, with their role and whether they can upload and share files there (canShare). Uploading and creating links or file requests only work where canShare is true.

tools.name: tarkle_list_files
tools.description: List files already in a workspace library (newest first), with fileId, type, size, sha256 when Tarkle recorded one, and their tags and description. query matches the file name and, where descriptions exist, the description. tag lists only files with that tag, anywhere in the library (see tarkle_list_tags). Use the fileId values with tarkle_read_file, tarkle_get_download_link or tarkle_create_transfer. When nextCursor is returned, more files may follow: call again with the same inputs and that cursor. A short page, or one that shows no files, is not the end while nextCursor is there (files private to someone else are left out).

query.description: Text to look for in file names and, where files have one, descriptions.

limit.description: How many files to return per page. Defaults to 25.

folderId.description: Only files directly in this folder (from tarkle_list_folders). Omit for the whole library.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous answer, to get the next page. Keep the other inputs the same.

tag.description: Only list files that have this tag, anywhere in the library. Tags come from tarkle_list_tags.

tools.name: tarkle_search_files
tools.description: Search the words INSIDE the workspace's files (PDF, Word, text, Markdown, subtitles, scanned pages, and what is said in audio and video recordings) and get the best matching passages, each with fileId, name, page and a snippet; a recording's snippet starts with its time as [m:ss] and has no page. Read more of a hit with tarkle_read_file. coverage says how many files were searched and how many cannot be searched as text (pictures, archives, recordings with no speech) or are still waiting: if waiting is above 0, search again. Only files this person can open are searched. Searching can use a few of the workspace's AI credits to finish preparing files for search, and a scan or recording Tarkle has not read yet is read first, which also uses AI credits.

query.description: The words to look for inside the files.

limit.description: How many passages to return. Defaults to 8.

folderId.description: Only search inside this folder and its subfolders (from tarkle_list_folders).

tools.name: tarkle_read_file
tools.description: Read the text of one file by fileId (from tarkle_search_files or tarkle_list_files), about 12,000 characters per call. For a PDF choose pages with fromPage and toPage; truncated says more follows. An audio or video recording is read as its transcript, each line starting with its time as [m:ss]. note says what is missing when only part of a file could be read. A file Tarkle cannot read is refused with the reason (still being read: ask again; no speech; a format it cannot open; too large). Reading a file Tarkle has already read uses no credits; a scan or recording it has not read yet is read first, which uses the workspace's AI credits.

fileId.description: The id of a file, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_search_files.

fromPage.description: First page to read, counting from 1. Applies to PDFs.

toPage.description: Last page to read. Applies to PDFs.

tools.name: tarkle_get_download_link
tools.description: Get a short-lived link to the exact bytes of one file (fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_search_files), for any file type: a PDF, a picture, audio, video or an archive. Fetch the link at once with a plain GET (no Authorization header); it stops working after expiresInSeconds, so ask again rather than keeping it, and never show it to anyone else. sha256, when known, is the file's SHA-256 recorded by Tarkle, so you can check the bytes you fetched. Only files this person can open. The download is recorded in the workspace's activity log.

fileId.description: The id of a file, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_search_files.

tools.name: tarkle_ask
tools.description: Ask a question and get an answer written from the workspace's files, with the sources it used: numbered [n] in the answer, each with fileId, name and pages. Use it when you want Tarkle to read the files for you; to read them yourself use tarkle_search_files and tarkle_read_file, which write no answer: reading a file Tarkle has already read uses no credits, searching can use a few to finish preparing files for search, and a scan or recording Tarkle has not read yet is read first, which uses AI credits. This SPENDS CREDITS like a question in Ask about files (the workspace's plan credits or its own AI key pay; the answer says how many were used; deep is Pro only). It only reads: nothing is changed. Only files this person can open are read. folderId limits the question to one folder; mode deep is slower and thorough. Nothing is saved between calls: for a follow-up send the earlier questions and answers as history.

question.description: The question to answer from the workspace's files.

folderId.description: Only answer from this folder and its subfolders (from tarkle_list_folders).

mode.description: basic (default) is quick; deep reads more and costs more (Pro plans and own AI keys).

role.description: Who wrote this message: the person (user) or Tarkle (assistant).

content.description: The text of the earlier question or answer.

history.description: Earlier questions and answers of this conversation, oldest first, so a follow-up makes sense. Each is charged as input.

tools.name: tarkle_extract_data
tools.description: Start reading chosen fields out of up to 10 PDFs or pictures (fileIds from tarkle_list_files): an invoice's supplier, number, dates and total, a contract's parties and terms. Give a ready-made template (invoice, receipt, contract) or your own fields (a name, a type of text, number, date, yes_no, choice or table, with options for a choice and columns for a table; up to 20). The reading continues in the background: this returns a runId and the credits quoted; call tarkle_get_extraction with it a few seconds later (about 3 to 6 seconds a page) for the answers, each with the page it was read from. A value the document does not state is empty, never guessed. THIS SPENDS CREDITS (about 20 a page, charged for each file once read). Up to any number of pages (only the credits limit a run); a password-protected or unreadable file is refused. Only files this person can open are read.

fileIds.description: Ids of the files to read, from tarkle_list_files. They must be PDFs or PNG, JPG or TIFF pictures.

template.description: A ready-made set of fields. Send this or fields.

name.description: The name of the field, used to label its answer.

description.description: What to look for, to help Tarkle find the value.

type.description: The kind of value the field holds.

options.description: For a choice field: the values it can take.

columns.description: For a table field: the names of the columns.

fields.description: Your own fields. Send this or template.

mode.description: standard is used when omitted. deep costs about twice as much and is for hard documents.

tools.name: tarkle_get_extraction
tools.description: The state of a run started with tarkle_extract_data (or the suggestion of tarkle_split_document, which answers with its suggested parts): status (queued, running, succeeded, failed) and, per file, its status and answers: one entry per field in the order asked, with value (as the document writes it), normalized (a plain number or an ISO date when the field is one), confidence, the page it was read from, and rows for a table. Corrections a person made in Tarkle are applied. While the status is queued or running, call again in a few seconds. Reading only: it costs nothing. A person sees their own runs; an owner or admin sees all of the workspace's.

runId.description: The runId returned by tarkle_extract_data or tarkle_split_document.

tools.name: tarkle_split_document
tools.description: Cut one PDF (fileId from tarkle_list_files) that holds several documents into separate PDFs, one per document, saved into the workspace's Split parts folder. Three ways: (1) send parts ([{ title, pages: [1,2,3] }]: every page in one part at most, in the order to write them) to cut now, which costs nothing and answers with the new files; (2) send sections ([{ name: 'Invoice', description: 'a bill with a total to pay', partitionKey: 'invoice number' }], up to 20; the partitionKey is what tells two documents of the same kind apart, so two invoices in a row become two parts; optional rules change how pages are assigned) to have the pages classified: this spends credits (about 21 a page), returns a runId, and the suggested parts are read with tarkle_get_extraction a few seconds later; (3) send the runId of a finished suggestion (optionally with your own parts) to write its parts as files. Each new file can then be read with tarkle_extract_data. Only a PDF; a password-protected or unreadable file is refused. Only files this person can open are cut.

fileId.description: The PDF to cut (from tarkle_list_files). Not needed with a runId.

runId.description: A finished suggestion: write its parts (or the parts you send) as files.

name.description: The kind of document to look for, for example Invoice.

description.description: A short note on what this kind of document looks like, to help tell it from others.

partitionKey.description: What tells two documents of this kind apart, such as 'invoice number': with it, two invoices that follow each other are two parts.

sections.description: Kinds of document to look for. Spends credits.

rules.description: With sections: your own rules for where documents begin and end (for example 'keep every contract together'). Leave out for the default.

tableCutoff.description: With sections: preserve reads whole tables when classifying (slower; for identifiers deep inside long tables).

title.description: The title of this part, used to name its file.

pages.description: The page numbers that go into this part, with 1 as the first page.

parts.description: The cut to make: a title and the pages (1 is the first) of each part.

tools.name: tarkle_get_activity
tools.description: The workspace's activity log, newest first: uploads, downloads, views of links and files, moves, renames, deletes, invitations, transfers, brand and API-key changes, each with who did it, when, which item and where it came from (the app, the API, an AI agent, Slack or a shared link). Defaults to the last 7 days and 50 events; limit goes up to 500. Filters: actor (a name), action (for example upload, download, view) and resource (file, folder, transfer). Sign-ins are logged too (action login, shown as “Signed in”): a visit after 30 quiet minutes counts as one. To give the person a PDF or CSV, save the rows with tarkle_upload_text.

days.description: How many days back to look. Defaults to 7.

limit.description: How many events to return. Defaults to 50.

actor.description: Part of the name of the person who did the action.

action.description: The action to show, for example upload, download or view.

resource.description: The kind of item to show, for example file, folder or transfer.

tools.name: tarkle_get_received_emails
tools.description: The files that arrived by email (Email to Tarkle), newest first: who sent each email (address and contact name), when, which inbox (the workspace address, shown to owners, admins and members but not viewers, or the caller's own personal address; never another member's), the subject, how many files, the folder it went into and each file with its name, size, type, when it was saved and its index state (ready, reading, partial or not_readable). To say what a ready file is about, read it with tarkle_read_file or find passages with tarkle_search_files using its fileId; a recording comes back as a transcript with [m:ss] times. A file still being read has no summary yet: say so. Filters: inbox (all, workspace, personal), sender, days (default 30), limit (default 10, up to 50). Older emails may list no files.

inbox.description: Which address to read: the workspace address, your own personal address, or both. Both are read when omitted.

sender.description: Part of the sender's email address.

days.description: How many days back to look. Defaults to 30.

limit.description: How many emails to return. Defaults to 10.

includeNotSaved.description: Also list emails that have no saved files. By default only emails with files are listed.

tools.name: tarkle_report_feedback
tools.description: Tell the Tarkle team what went wrong or what is missing while you used this connector, so it can be improved. Use it when a tool failed in a way that looks like a bug, when you needed a tool or option that does not exist, or when something was hard to use. Write like a good bug report: what the person asked for, what you called (tool name and the shape of the input), what you expected, what happened (the error code and text), and a proposed fix if you have one. The text goes to the Tarkle team together with the signed-in person's name and email (they get the reply). Never include file contents, passwords, tokens, links with secrets or other people's personal data. Send one report per problem, at most a few per session. Tell the person you sent it.

kind.description: bug: something failed or behaved wrongly. missing_tool: you needed a tool or option that does not exist. improvement: it worked but could be better. question: you could not tell how something should work.

summary.description: One line saying what the problem is.

details.description: What the person asked for, what you called (tool and input shape, without secrets), what you expected, what happened (error code and text).

proposedFix.description: What you think should change, if you have an idea.

tool.description: The tool this is about, for example tarkle_list_files.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's id, from tarkle_list_workspaces, if the problem is about one workspace.

tools.name: tarkle_list_folders
tools.description: List the folders directly inside one folder of a workspace library (the library root when parentFolderId is omitted), or find folders by name anywhere in the library with query (with parentFolderId too, only its direct subfolders). Use the returned folderId as parentFolderId to go deeper, or as folderId when uploading or listing files. When nextCursor is returned, more folders follow: call again with the same inputs and that cursor. Protected folders (team, file request, active share) are marked and may refuse new files. Each folder has its tags and description.

parentFolderId.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

query.description: Part of a folder name, for example "invoices". Matches anywhere in the library unless parentFolderId is set.

limit.description: How many folders to return per page. Defaults to 200, or 50 when query is set.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous answer. Keep the other inputs the same.

tools.name: tarkle_create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder in a workspace library (inside parentFolderId, or at the root). Returns folderId. The same rules as the app apply: a name already used in that folder is refused (NAME_TAKEN, so list the folders first and reuse it), and protected folders cannot take new folders.

name.description: The name of the new folder.

parentFolderId.description: The folder to create it in, from tarkle_list_folders. The library root is used when omitted.

visibility.description: private (default): only the person, whoever they share it with, and the workspace owners and admins. workspace: every member of the workspace can see it.

tools.name: tarkle_list_bin
tools.description: List what is in the workspace's recovery bin that this person may see, newest first: files (fileId) and folders (folderId), each with the day it was binned. A folder is listed once, not every file inside it. Use the ids with tarkle_restore_from_bin; an item past the plan's bin retention is refused there. Up to 40 items.

limit.description: How many items to return. Defaults to 25.

tools.name: tarkle_rename_file
tools.description: Rename one file. The same rules as the app apply: a name already used in that folder is refused (NAME_TAKEN), and the file extension is part of the name. A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

fileId.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

name.description: The new full name, including the extension.

tools.name: tarkle_update_details
tools.description: Add or remove tags and set or clear the description of one file (fileId) or folder (folderId); send exactly one of them, and at least one of addTags, removeTags or description. Tags: up to 20 an item, each up to 32 characters once cleaned: letters, numbers, - or _ (a leading # is dropped, spaces become -, stored lowercase); reuse the workspace's tags from tarkle_list_tags. Description: plain text up to 500 characters once spaces at the ends are removed, or null to clear it. Whoever may rename the item may change these; a Tarkle system folder or a folder used by an active file request is refused with the reason. Answers with the item (id, name, tags and description) after the change.

fileId.description: The id of a file, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

folderId.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

addTags.description: Tags to add, for example ["invoice", "2026"]. Existing tags are kept.

removeTags.description: Tags to take off. Other tags are kept.

description.description: The new plain-text description, or null to clear it. Spaces at the ends and control characters are removed first, and the cleaned text can be up to 500 characters. Leave it out to keep the current description.

tools.name: tarkle_list_tags
tools.description: The tags used on files and folders in a workspace, most used first, with how many items carry each. Only items this person can open are counted. Reuse these tags with tarkle_update_details, and find files by tag with tarkle_list_files (tag).

limit.description: How many tags to return. Defaults to 100.

tools.name: tarkle_rename_tag
tools.description: Rename one tag on every file and folder in a workspace (name is the new tag). If an item already has the new tag, the two merge. Up to 500 items; a tag on more is refused. Only workspace Owners and Admins; an Admin with admin privacy changes only the items they can open, and the answer says how many were left out (skippedPrivate). Items that cannot be changed (a system folder, a folder used by an active file request) are listed in failed. To change the tags of one item use tarkle_update_details. A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

tag.description: The tag to rename, from tarkle_list_tags.

name.description: The new tag. If an item already has it, the two tags merge.

tools.name: tarkle_delete_tag
tools.description: Take one tag off every file and folder in a workspace. The files and folders stay; only the tag goes. Up to 500 items. Only workspace Owners and Admins. Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing and says how many items carry the tag; show that to the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode. Items that cannot be changed are listed in failed. A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

tag.description: The tag to remove, from tarkle_list_tags.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved removing the tag everywhere.

tools.name: tarkle_move_file
tools.description: Move one file into a folder (folderId from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder), or to the library root with folderId null. The file keeps its name; a name already used in the destination is refused (NAME_TAKEN). Moving into a folder can change who can see the file, because a folder decides that. A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

fileId.description: The id of a file, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The destination folder, or null for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_rename_folder
tools.description: Rename one folder (folderId from tarkle_list_folders). A protected folder (team folder, file request, system folder) is refused with the reason, and so is a name already used next to it (NAME_TAKEN). Everything inside goes with it.

folderId.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

name.description: The folder's new name.

tools.name: tarkle_move_folder
tools.description: Move one folder, with everything in it, into another folder (parentFolderId), or to the library root with parentFolderId null. A folder cannot go into itself or one of its own subfolders (INVALID_DESTINATION). Moving can change who can see what is inside, because a folder decides that. A protected folder (team folder, file request, system folder) is refused with the reason, and so is a name already used next to it (NAME_TAKEN). Everything inside goes with it.

folderId.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

parentFolderId.description: The destination folder, or null for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_copy_file
tools.description: Copy one file inside Tarkle (nothing is downloaded or uploaded again). folderId: the destination folder, null for the library root, left out for the same folder. name: the copy's full name with its extension, left out for the same name; a name already used there is refused (NAME_TAKEN), a copy is never renamed silently, so copying into the same folder needs a new name. The copy counts toward storage and the plan's file size limit (FILE_TOO_LARGE, STORAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). Folders cannot be copied.

fileId.description: The file's fileId, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The destination folder, null for the library root, or leave out for the same folder.

name.description: The copy's full name, including the extension.

tools.name: tarkle_list_versions
tools.description: The earlier versions of one file, newest first (Pro): versionId, number, name, sizeBytes, savedAt, replacedAt, keptUntil (after that it is gone), and restorable (false for a version someone deleted, which stays listed until it expires). current is the file as it is now. A Free workspace is refused. Anyone who can see the file can list its versions.

fileId.description: The file's fileId, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

tools.name: tarkle_restore_version
tools.description: Make an earlier version (versionId from tarkle_list_versions) the current file again (Pro). Nothing is lost: the file as it is now is kept as a version, and the restored copy counts toward storage. Needs a role that may edit files. A file used by a share link is refused (CONFLICT) unless updateShareLinks is true, because the link then delivers the restored version: ask the person first. Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

fileId.description: The file's fileId, from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

versionId.description: The version to restore, from tarkle_list_versions for the same file.

updateShareLinks.description: true: also change what share links holding this file deliver. Only after the person agreed.

confirmationCode.description: The confirmationCode from the first answer of this tool for the same inputs. Send it only after the user approved.

tools.name: tarkle_edit_pdf
tools.description: Page tools on a PDF, saved as a NEW PDF: mergeFileIds (other PDFs appended in order, up to 9), keep or remove (pages like 1-3,5; not both), order (a new page order like [3,1,2]), rotate ([{pages, degrees 90, 180 or 270}]), crop (millimetres off each side, optional pages; the cut-off part is hidden, not deleted), blankAfter and blankAtStart (blank pages), pageNumbers (true, or {position, start}), watermark (text drawn over every page; it hides nothing underneath and is NOT redaction), title, author. They apply in that order; give at least one. name sets the new file's name (default "<name> (edited).pdf"). The file is never changed: a NEW file is saved next to it (or in folderId) and its fileId is returned; a taken name is refused (NAME_TAKEN). The same function and limits as the Tarkle chat and the API: 40 MB a PDF, a password-protected or damaged PDF is refused with the reason.

fileId.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

mergeFileIds.description: Other PDFs to append after this one, in the order given. Each is a fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

keep.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

remove.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

order.description: The page numbers in the order the pages should appear, for example [3,1,2].

pages.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

degrees.description: How far to turn the pages, in degrees.

rotate.description: Rotations to apply. Each item names the pages to turn and the angle.

top.description: Millimetres to cut off the top edge.

right.description: Millimetres to cut off the right edge.

bottom.description: Millimetres to cut off the bottom edge.

left.description: Millimetres to cut off the left edge.

pages.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

crop.description: Margins to cut off the pages, in millimetres. At least one side must be above 0. The cut-off part is hidden, not deleted.

blankAfter.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

blankAtStart.description: true: add a blank page before the first page.

position.description: Where on the page the number goes. bottom-center when omitted.

start.description: The number printed on the first page. 1 when omitted.

pageNumbers.description: true adds page numbers. An object also sets where they go and the first number.

watermark.description: Text drawn diagonally over every page. It hides nothing underneath and is not redaction.

title.description: Sets the title in the PDF's document properties.

author.description: Sets the author in the PDF's document properties.

name.description: The new file's name; the .pdf extension is added or corrected.

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The folder for the new file; null for the library root; omit to keep the source's folder.

tools.name: tarkle_convert_file
tools.description: Converts a file into a NEW file. "to": text (a PDF's text as .txt), images (each page as PNG or JPG in a .zip, up to 30 pages; imageFormat), split (a .zip of PDFs; ranges "each" or "1-3,4-6"), word (the text as a .docx: headings, paragraphs, bullets, tables; layout and pictures are not kept), excel (the tables found by position as a .xlsx; none found is refused), pdf (fileId is a picture, with moreFileIds for more pictures and pageSize fit, a4 or letter; or fileId is ONE Word, Excel or PowerPoint file, converted by LibreOffice in an isolated sandbox, which can take up to about half a minute), ocr (a searchable PDF from a scan; English, up to 8 scanned pages a run), redact (terms: the exact texts to black out, and/or emails true: every page with a match becomes a picture so the text is gone for good; every term must exist; a scan cannot be redacted), compress (level light, medium or strong). pages limits text, images, word, excel, ocr and redact to some pages. Adding or removing a PDF password is NOT available here (a password would pass through the conversation): use the Tarkle API or the chat. The file is never changed: a NEW file is saved next to it (or in folderId) and its fileId is returned; a taken name is refused (NAME_TAKEN). The same function and limits as the Tarkle chat and the API: 40 MB a PDF, a password-protected or damaged PDF is refused with the reason.

fileId.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

to.description: The kind of file to make. The other fields that apply depend on it; see the tool description.

pages.description: Which pages to use, as page numbers and ranges counted from the first page, for example 1-3,5,8-.

imageFormat.description: Picture format when converting to images. png when omitted.

ranges.description: When converting to split: how to cut the PDF, either each (one PDF per page) or ranges like 1-3,4-6. each when omitted.

moreFileIds.description: When converting pictures to pdf: more pictures to add after the source, in the order given. Each is a fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

pageSize.description: Page size when converting pictures to pdf. fit when omitted.

terms.description: When converting to redact: the exact texts to black out. Every term must be found in the file.

emails.description: When converting to redact: true also blacks out every email address.

level.description: When converting to compress: how strongly to compress. medium when omitted.

name.description: Name for the new file. Tarkle sets the right file extension. When omitted, the name is made from the source file's name.

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: Folder to save the new file in, from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder. Use null for the library root. When omitted, the new file goes in the source file's folder.

tools.name: tarkle_create_document
tools.description: Writes a NEW document from content you give: format pdf, docx or pptx take markdown (for pptx an outline: "# Title" is the title slide and its first line the subtitle, each "## Heading" is a slide, bullets become bullet points, a table gets its own slide); md takes markdown; xlsx and csv take table (columns and rows of text, up to 12 columns and 500 rows; Excel keeps numbers as numbers and codes with leading zeros as text). Up to 60,000 characters of Markdown. Gather the facts first and write only what they showed. sources: ids of the files the document is based on (up to 10): a true Sources list is added from their real names. name is required (the extension is added). A NEW file is saved (the source or template is never changed) and its fileId is returned; a taken name is refused (NAME_TAKEN). The same generators and limits as the Tarkle chat and the API.

name.description: Name for the new file. The extension for format is added.

format.description: The kind of document to write. Give markdown for pdf, docx, pptx and md, and table for xlsx and csv.

markdown.description: The document's content as Markdown. For pptx, write an outline: # Title is the title slide and each ## Heading is a slide.

rows.description: The table rows. Each row is a list of text values in column order.

table.description: The content for xlsx and csv: column headings and rows of text.

items.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

sources.description: Files the document is based on, each a fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin. A Sources list built from their names is added to the document.

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The folder for the file; null or omit for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_fill_template
tools.description: fileId is a Word (.docx) template with {placeholders}; values maps each placeholder name, exactly as written in the template, to text, or to a list of rows for a repeated block or table row (for example items: [{ item: "Setup", price: "100" }]). Every placeholder needs a value and every value a placeholder; otherwise the call is refused and names what is missing, unused and the template's own placeholders. name sets the new file's name (default "<template> (filled).docx"). A NEW file is saved (the source or template is never changed) and its fileId is returned; a taken name is refused (NAME_TAKEN). The same generators and limits as the Tarkle chat and the API.

fileId.description: The Word (.docx) template, as a fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

values.description: Maps each placeholder name in the template, exactly as written there, to its text, or to a list of rows for a repeated block or table row.

name.description: Name for the new file. When omitted, "<template name> (filled).docx".

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The folder for the new file; null for the library root; omit to keep the template's folder.

tools.name: tarkle_edit_office_file
tools.description: Saves changes to a COPY of the file. The kind of file decides the fields: .docx: edits ([{find, replace}], exact text, up to 50), inserts (paragraphs, a table, or a picture by fileId of a PNG, JPG or GIF, placed after some text or at the end), trackChanges (the changes become tracked changes by Tarkle that the person accepts or rejects in Word); .pptx: edits ([{find, replace}] on every slide where the text appears); .xlsx: cells ([{sheet, cell, value}], up to 100; an empty value clears the cell) and appendRows ([{sheet, rows}], up to 200 rows). Read the file first and copy the text to find exactly; every text, anchor or sheet named must exist or the call is refused and says which. A cell with a formula, a merged cell, or a workbook with charts, pictures, pivot tables or macros is refused. name sets the new file's name (default "<name> (edited).<ext>"). A NEW file is saved (the source or template is never changed) and its fileId is returned; a taken name is refused (NAME_TAKEN). The same generators and limits as the Tarkle chat and the API.

fileId.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

find.description: The exact text to find. It must exist in the file or the call is refused.

replace.description: The text to put in its place.

edits.description: For .docx and .pptx: text replacements. Each finds exact text and replaces it.

after.description: Existing text to insert after. When omitted, the content goes at the end of the document.

rows.description: The table rows. Each row is a list of text values in column order.

fileId.description: The picture to insert (a PNG, JPG or GIF), as a fileId from tarkle_list_files.

widthInches.description: Width of the picture in inches. When omitted, the picture keeps its own size, scaled down if it is too big for the page.

inserts.description: For .docx: content to add after some text, or at the end of the document.

trackChanges.description: For .docx: true saves the changes as tracked changes that the person can accept or reject in Word.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet. It must exist in the workbook.

cell.description: The cell address, for example B2.

value.description: The new value. Empty text clears the cell.

sheet.description: The name of the sheet to add the rows to. It must exist in the workbook.

rows.description: The rows to add. Each row is a list of values in column order.

appendRows.description: For .xlsx: rows to add at the end of a sheet.

name.description: Name for the new file. When omitted, "<name> (edited).<ext>".

anyOf.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderId.description: The folder for the new file; null for the library root; omit to keep the source's folder.

tools.name: tarkle_delete_files
tools.description: Move up to 20 files to the recovery bin of a workspace. This is the app's delete: nothing is erased, and tarkle_restore_from_bin brings a file back within the plan's bin retention. Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing and lists the files and the workspace; show them to the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode. A file held by a share link is NOT deleted (that would also delete the link); tell the user to remove the link in Tarkle. Owners and Admins; other members only for files they uploaded themselves. A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

items.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

fileIds.description: The files to move to the bin, each a fileId from tarkle_list_files.

confirmationCode.description: The confirmationCode from the first answer of this tool for the same inputs. Send it only after the user approved moving these files to the bin.

tools.name: tarkle_restore_from_bin
tools.description: Bring up to 20 files and folders back from the bin (ids from tarkle_list_bin). Each returns to the folder it was in, if that folder still exists (otherwise restore the folder first: PARENT_UNAVAILABLE), and only within the plan's bin retention (EXPIRED). A name that is now taken is refused. Owners and Admins; other members only for files they uploaded themselves (folders: Owners and Admins). A file that is protected (team folder, file request, system folder), sold, or held by a share link is refused with the reason.

items.description: A fileId from tarkle_list_files or tarkle_list_bin.

fileIds.description: Files to restore, each a fileId from tarkle_list_bin.

items.description: A folder id from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder.

folderIds.description: Folders to restore, each a folderId from tarkle_list_bin.

tools.name: tarkle_get_upload_page
tools.description: Use when the file is not reachable from this environment (for example a chat attachment or a file on the user's own device). Returns a Tarkle page where the user picks the file in their browser. With folderId (and workspaceId) the files go into that folder instead of the library root; with fileName a single chosen file is saved under that name (its extension is kept when fileName has none). After they confirm it finished, call tarkle_list_files with the same folderId to find the new file, then tarkle_create_transfer.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's id from tarkle_list_workspaces. When omitted and exactly one workspace allows you to share files, that workspace is used.

folderId.description: Folder to save the file in (from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder). Omit for the library root.

fileName.description: The name to save a single chosen file under, for example "Signed contract.pdf".

tools.name: tarkle_upload_text
tools.description: Save text you already hold (a report, notes, markdown, CSV, JSON, HTML, a notebook export) as a file in a Tarkle workspace. Use this when you have no file on disk and no shell: the content goes in the call and Tarkle stores it. Up to 3 MB of text. A fileName without an extension gets .md. Returns fileId for tarkle_create_transfer. For a binary file (PDF, image, video) use tarkle_upload_from_url or tarkle_get_upload_page.

fileName.description: Name for the file. Without an extension, .md is added.

content.description: The text to save as the file's content.

contentType.description: Optional MIME type; guessed from the file name when omitted.

folderId.description: Folder to save the file in (from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder). Omit for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_upload_file
tools.description: Save a small file of any type (a PDF, a picture, a spreadsheet, a zip) that you hold in this conversation as a file in a Tarkle workspace, sent as base64 in contentBase64. Up to 2.5 MB after decoding. For text use tarkle_upload_text; for a file at a public https address use tarkle_upload_from_url; for a larger file on disk use tarkle_start_upload; for a file only the person has, tarkle_get_upload_page. fileName needs an extension. Send sha256 (hex) of the file if you know it: Tarkle refuses bytes that do not match, and the answer gives the sha256 of what it stored. Without folderId the file goes to the library root. Returns fileId (for tarkle_create_transfer), fileName, sizeBytes, status and sha256.

fileName.description: Name for the file, including its extension, for example "split-check.pdf".

contentBase64.description: The file's content, base64 encoded. Do not add a data: prefix.

contentType.description: MIME type of the file. When omitted, it is guessed from the file name.

sha256.description: SHA-256 checksum of the file, if you know it. The upload is refused when it does not match the decoded content.

folderId.description: Folder to save the file in (from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder). Omit for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_upload_from_url
tools.description: Tarkle downloads a file from a public https address (or from a file the user attached in ChatGPT) and saves it in a workspace. Use this when you have a link to the file but no disk or shell. The address must be reachable without a sign-in; up to 50 MB (use tarkle_get_upload_page for bigger files). Pass url, or file for an attachment. Returns fileId for tarkle_create_transfer.

url.description: Public https address of the file.

download_url.description: The attachment's download address, given by ChatGPT.

file_id.description: ChatGPT's own id for the attachment. Not a Tarkle file id.

mime_type.description: The attachment's type as ChatGPT reports it, for example application/pdf.

file_name.description: The attachment's name as ChatGPT reports it.

file.description: A file the user attached in ChatGPT. Send it instead of url.

fileName.description: Name to save as; taken from the address when omitted.

contentType.description: MIME type to save the file with. When omitted, the attachment's mime_type or the type the remote server reports is used.

folderId.description: Folder to save the file in (from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder). Omit for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_start_upload
tools.description: Start uploading one file to a Tarkle workspace. Returns signed URLs for sending the bytes directly to storage with HTTP PUT (no Authorization header). Up to 1 GB is one URL; larger files are split into 512 MB parts (a 10 GB file is 20 URLs; ask for more with tarkle_get_upload_parts). The result includes the exact shell command. Size limit: your plan's per-file limit when the client runs on the person's computer (Claude Code, Droid, Cursor); 5 GB in web chat apps (ChatGPT, Claude.ai), which should use tarkle_get_upload_page for larger files. If you cannot run shell commands or reach the network, do not use this tool: use tarkle_upload_text (text you hold), tarkle_upload_from_url (a public https address) or tarkle_get_upload_page. Then poll tarkle_get_upload_status.

fileName.description: Name to save the file under.

sizeBytes.description: The file's exact size in bytes. The upload fails if the bytes sent do not add up to this.

folderId.description: Folder to save the file in (from tarkle_list_folders or tarkle_create_folder). Omit for the library root.

tools.name: tarkle_get_upload_parts
tools.description: For multipart uploads: get fresh signed URLs for a range of parts, starting at fromPart (part numbers start at 1; fromPart defaults to 1). Also use this to retry a part whose URL expired. Returns uploads: a list with partNumber, url and contentLength for each part.

fromPart.description: The first part to get URLs for. 1 when omitted.

count.description: How many parts to get URLs for, counting from fromPart. 50 when omitted.

tools.name: tarkle_get_upload_status
tools.description: Check an upload. Once all bytes are uploaded this finishes the upload and returns fileId for tarkle_create_transfer, and sha256: the SHA-256 Tarkle read back from what it stored (files up to 100 MB), to compare with your own file. Safe to call repeatedly.

tools.name: tarkle_list_transfers
tools.description: The workspace's existing share links, newest first: transfers, video and audio links, galleries and Feedback boards. Each has its transferId, title, kind, link, status (active, disabled, used for a link that opened once, expired), expiry, whether it has a password, view and download counts, and createdByYou. Owners and admins see every link in the workspace, a member sees the ones they created, a viewer sees none. query matches the title; kind is one of transfer, video, audio, gallery, canvas. Pass nextCursor back as cursor for the next page. No password, recipient list or file contents are returned.

query.description: Text to look for in the share link's title.

kind.description: Only list share links of this kind.

limit.description: How many share links to return in one page. 25 when omitted.

cursor.description: The nextCursor from the previous answer, to get the next page.

tools.name: tarkle_whoami
tools.description: The signed-in person this connection acts as (userId, name, email), the organization they own with its plan (free, pro or agency; null when they own none), and what this connection may do (its permissions). Use tarkle_list_workspaces for the workspaces and the person's role in each.

tools.name: tarkle_get_usage
tools.description: One workspace's storage (usedBytes, limitBytes, freeBytes, bytes by kind of file, region, and how it gets its space: own, shared from the organization's pool, or assigned) and the AI credits it can still spend today and this month (aiCredits: payer tarkle or own_key, today, thisMonth, the plan allowance, the workspace caps, extra credits, when each window resets). A null limit means no limit. Asking questions (tarkle_ask) and reading data with Studio spend credits. Reading a file Tarkle has already read does not; searching can use a few credits to finish preparing files for search, and a scan or recording not read yet is read first, which uses credits.

tools.name: tarkle_create_transfer
tools.description: Create a PUBLIC share link for files already in the workspace: anyone with the link can view and download. No email is sent. kind 'audio' or 'video' creates the matching player page. Asks for confirmation first: the first call creates nothing and describes the link; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

fileIds.description: The ids of the files to put in the share link, from tarkle_list_files.

title.description: The title of the share link.

description.description: An optional description of the share link.

kind.description: What kind of link to make. Use audio or video for a player page. Files is used when omitted.

confirmationCode.description: The confirmationCode from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved the public link.

tools.name: tarkle_create_gallery
tools.description: Turn a folder of photos (folderId from tarkle_list_folders) into a public gallery at /g/<slug>. The photos are the JPG, PNG and WebP files directly in the folder, up to 500. Without a price (the default) it's a free gallery: everyone can view it, watermarked only if watermark is true. With a price it's a paid gallery: visitors see every photo as a lower-resolution watermarked preview (previewMode "all", the default) or only the first previewCount photos with the rest blurred ("first"); they pay with PayPal or card, whichever the workspace connected, then download every original for 30 days, with no account -- needs Pro and PayPal or Stripe connected in Settings > Integrations, otherwise the answer says what to do. Returns galleryUrl (/g/..., browse) and, only for a paid gallery, payUrl (/pay/..., opens checkout directly; after paying the buyer lands on the unlocked gallery). Creating it sends no email; a paid sale gets the buyer a receipt with their own download link, and the workspace owner a sale notice. Asks for confirmation first: the first call creates nothing and describes the gallery (photo count, price if any, client); ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

folderId.description: The folder of photos to share, from tarkle_list_folders.

price.description: The price in the currency's main unit, for example "600" or "49.90". Omit it for a free gallery.

currency.description: The currency the buyer pays in. One of USD, EUR, GBP, CAD, AUD, CHF, SEK, NOK, DKK, PLN, CZK, NZD, SGD, HKD, MXN. Only used with a price; USD when omitted.

watermark.description: Only for a free gallery -- a paid gallery is always watermarked until bought. Default false.

clientName.description: Who the gallery is for. It is shown on the gallery as "For <name>".

previewMode.description: Only for a paid gallery. "all" shows every photo as a watermarked preview; "first" shows only the first previewCount photos and blurs the rest. "all" is used when omitted.

previewCount.description: With previewMode "first": how many photos show before payment. Default 3.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved sharing (and, with a price, selling) this folder.

tools.name: tarkle_get_gallery_status
tools.description: Show a paid gallery's sales (galleryId from tarkle_create_gallery): its gallery and pay links, price, and every purchase (status completed or refunded, amount, currency, buyer name and email, paid_at, access_until). Only a completed purchase means the client paid; never tell the user someone paid without one. Not useful on a free gallery -- it has no purchases.

tools.name: tarkle_deliver_transfer_to_contacts
tools.description: Add contacts (contactId from tarkle_list_contacts) to a transfer (transferId from tarkle_create_transfer) so it shows in their client portal. No email is sent; a contact sees it only while their portal access is on (tarkle_set_portal_access). Plain file transfers only; a paid transfer is refused. Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

transferId.description: The transfer's id, from tarkle_create_transfer or tarkle_list_transfers.

contactIds.description: The ids of the contacts to show the transfer to, from tarkle_list_contacts.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved showing this transfer to these contacts.

tools.name: tarkle_update_transfer
tools.description: Change a plain transfer (transferId from tarkle_create_transfer). viewOnly true: the people it is delivered to can only view its files; false: they can download them. expiresAt: an ISO date in the future (at most three years ahead), or null for no expiry. A paid transfer is refused. Turning view only OFF asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

transferId.description: The transfer's id, from tarkle_create_transfer or tarkle_list_transfers.

viewOnly.description: true: people can only view the files. false: they can also download them. Left unchanged when omitted.

expiresAt.description: When the transfer expires, as an ISO date in the future. Send null for no expiry. Left unchanged when omitted.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved letting people download these files.

tools.name: tarkle_create_file_request
tools.description: Create a file request with a PUBLIC submission link: anyone with the link can upload files into the destination folder, and no email is sent to anyone (this tool only ever creates the public, no-organization kind of request -- it cannot target a client organization or trigger that organization-email flow). Returns the request ID, the public submission URL, and the destination/request folder IDs. Asks for confirmation first: the first call creates nothing and describes the request; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

title.description: The title of the file request.

description.description: An optional description shown to people who open the request.

destinationFolderId.description: The folder where submitted files go, from tarkle_list_folders.

expiresAt.description: When the request expires, as an ISO date and time.

confirmationCode.description: The confirmationCode from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved the public upload link.

tools.name: tarkle_close_file_request
tools.description: Close a file request so its public link stops accepting uploads. Files already submitted stay. Reversible with tarkle_reopen_file_request. Get requestId from tarkle_list_file_requests.

requestId.description: The file request's id, from tarkle_list_file_requests.

tools.name: tarkle_reopen_file_request
tools.description: Reopen a closed file request so its public link accepts uploads again (anyone with the link can upload). Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

requestId.description: The file request's id, from tarkle_list_file_requests.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved reopening this request.

tools.name: tarkle_delete_file_request
tools.description: Permanently delete a file request and its public link. The request folder and the files already submitted are kept in the library; only the request itself and the link go. Cannot be undone. Asks for confirmation first: the first call deletes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

requestId.description: The file request's id, from tarkle_list_file_requests.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved deleting this request.

tools.name: tarkle_list_file_requests
tools.description: List a workspace's file requests, newest first. Each request has its requestId, title, shortId, completed, isPublic, destinationFolderId, requestFolderId, expiresAt, createdAt and uploadsCount. Filter by status to see only active requests or only completed ones.

status.description: Which requests to list: only active ones, only completed ones, or all. All is used when omitted.

tools.name: tarkle_get_file_request_submissions
tools.description: List the files submitted to one file request (requestId from tarkle_list_file_requests). Returns the request's requestId, title and requestFolderId, and submissions: each with fileId, name, type, sizeBytes and submittedAt, newest first. Requires the workspaceId the request belongs to; a request ID from a different workspace is rejected rather than returning files.

requestId.description: The file request's id, from tarkle_list_file_requests.

tools.name: tarkle_list_brands
tools.description: List a workspace's brands. Each brand has its brandId, name, slug, isPublic, hasPassword, brandDomain and workspaceDomain. A brand's brandDomain is that brand's own public brand-page domain (if it has one), which is always different from workspaceDomain, the workspace's single transfer-link domain -- the two are never the same value.

tools.name: tarkle_list_contacts
tools.description: List a workspace's contacts (clients and leads), newest first, with their email, organization, and whether they have client portal access. Use contactId with the portal tools. Filter by part of a name or email.

query.description: Part of a name or email to filter by.

limit.description: The most contacts to return. 25 when omitted.

tools.name: tarkle_create_contact
tools.description: Add a contact to a workspace. Creates the record only: no email is sent and no login is made. A business contact (business true) belongs to an organization: give organizationName to create (or reuse) that organization with this contact as its owner (organizations are a Pro feature). To add an existing contact to an organization later: tarkle_add_contact_to_organization. To give portal access (which emails an invite): tarkle_set_portal_access after this. Fails if the email is already a contact.

organizationName.description: The organization to add the contact to. It is created if the workspace has none with this name.

business.description: true for a business contact; needs organizationName.

tools.name: tarkle_add_contact_to_organization
tools.description: Make an existing contact (contactId from tarkle_list_contacts) a business contact in an organization: the organization with this name in the workspace, or a new one with the contact as its owner. Organizations are a Pro feature. No email is sent. Needs a role that may edit contacts. Returns the updated contact: contactId, name, email, status, portalAccess, portalInvitedAt, portalSignedIn, organizations (organizationId, name), uploadLimitBytes (only when a limit is set) and createdAt.

organizationName.description: The name of the organization to add the contact to. It is created if the workspace has none with this name.

tools.name: tarkle_update_contact
tools.description: Change a contact's first or last name (contactId from tarkle_list_contacts). A name you leave out keeps its current value. No email is sent. Needs a role that may edit contacts.

firstName.description: The contact's new first name. The current one is kept when omitted.

lastName.description: The contact's new last name. The current one is kept when omitted.

tools.name: tarkle_set_portal_access
tools.description: Turn the client portal on or off for one contact (get contactId from tarkle_list_contacts). Turning it ON for the first time EMAILS the contact an invite to sign in to the workspace's portal (Pro feature). Turning it off sends nothing and takes effect at once. Asking to turn it on asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

enabled.description: true turns the client portal on for this contact. false turns it off.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved emailing this contact an invite.

tools.name: tarkle_resend_portal_invite
tools.description: Email a contact who already has portal access the sign-in link again. Fails if portal access is off. Asks for confirmation first: the first call sends nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved emailing this contact.

tools.name: tarkle_set_portal_storage_limit
tools.description: Set how much one contact may upload from their client portal, in GB (1 to 10000; the default is 5 GB). Only the contact's own uploads count. No email is sent.

limitGb.description: How much this contact may upload from their client portal, in GB.

tools.name: tarkle_list_team_folders
tools.description: List the team folders in a workspace that you can see (a team folder is a shared folder with its own people and storage budget; it is NOT the list of workspace members, see tarkle_list_members for that). Shows who can open each one (memberUserIds, user ids from tarkle_list_members), its storage budget (null means no limit), how much it uses, and the id of its main folder (use it as folderId in uploads). Listing works on any plan; creating and changing team folders needs a Pro, Agency or lifetime plan.

tools.name: tarkle_create_team_folder
tools.description: Create a team folder in a workspace: a shared folder with an optional storage budget. Only workspace Owners and Admins can, on a plan with team folders (Pro, Agency or a lifetime plan). access 'members' (default) is private to the people you add with tarkle_add_member_to_team_folder; 'everyone' is open to the whole workspace. No email is sent. Fails if a team folder with that name exists.

name.description: The team folder's name. It must not match an existing team folder in the workspace.

description.description: A short text saying what the team folder is for.

access.description: Who can open the folder. members means only the people you add with tarkle_add_member_to_team_folder; everyone means the whole workspace. Defaults to members.

budgetGb.description: The storage budget for the folder, in GB. Leave out for no limit.

tools.name: tarkle_set_team_folder_budget
tools.description: Set how much storage one team folder may use, in GB (1 to 1000000), or remove the limit with unlimited true. Works for a first budget and for editing one (get teamFolderId from tarkle_list_team_folders). Only workspace Owners and Admins can. The budget cannot be lower than what the folder already uses, and the budgets together cannot exceed the workspace's storage. The folder's people are not changed. No email is sent. Team folders need a Pro, Agency or lifetime plan.

If you have a tool for that DNS host (a Cloudflare, Vercel or registrar tool) you can add dns_guide.records yourself, with any proxy turned off, then call tarkle_check_brand_domain every 30 seconds until status is active. If not, read the steps to the person. The tool never changes DNS itself. Only workspace Owners and Admins can.

tools.description: Set the workspace's logo (kind logo, the default) or its browser tab icon (kind favicon, Pro). Give exactly one of contentBase64, url or fileId. PNG, JPEG or WebP, at least 24 px on each side; it is saved as a PNG of at most 512 px. The old image is replaced. Only workspace Owners and Admins can.

kind.description: Which image to set: the workspace logo or its favicon. If omitted, the logo is set.

contentBase64.description: The image bytes as base64, without a data: prefix. Use this, url or fileId.

url.description: A public https address of the image. Use this, contentBase64 or fileId.

fileId.description: The id of a file already in Tarkle, from tarkle_list_files or an upload tool. Use this, contentBase64 or url. Needs the workspace that holds the file (sourceWorkspaceId, or workspaceId on tools that have it).

sourceWorkspaceId.description: The workspace that holds the file, from tarkle_list_workspaces. Used with fileId. If omitted, workspaceId is used.

tools.name: tarkle_get_organization
tools.description: The organization the signed-in person owns or is an admin of (the account that holds the workspaces): name, description, website, business and contact emails, plan (free, pro or agency), your role in it, and whether it has a logo. Billing and plan changes stay in Tarkle.

tools.name: tarkle_update_organization
tools.description: Change only the fields you send of your organization: name (2 to 50 characters; also used on invoices), description, website (acme.com), businessEmail, contactEmail. Send null to clear a field other than name. The organization's owner or an admin can. Asks for confirmation first: the first call changes nothing; ask the user, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer.

name.description: The organization's new name. It is also used on invoices. It cannot be cleared.

description.description: A short description of the organization. Send null to clear it.

website.description: The organization's website, such as acme.com. Send null to clear it.

businessEmail.description: The organization's business email address. Send null to clear it.

contactEmail.description: The email address people can contact the organization on. Send null to clear it.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved these changes.

tools.name: tarkle_set_organization_logo
tools.description: Set the logo of the organization you own or are an admin of. Give exactly one of contentBase64, url or fileId. PNG, JPEG or WebP, at least 24 px on each side; it is saved as a PNG of at most 512 px. For fileId, send sourceWorkspaceId: the workspace that holds the file. Returns organizationId and saved (true).

contentBase64.description: The image bytes as base64, without a data: prefix. Use this, url or fileId.

url.description: A public https address of the image. Use this, contentBase64 or fileId.

fileId.description: The id of a file already in Tarkle, from tarkle_list_files or an upload tool. Use this, contentBase64 or url. Needs the workspace that holds the file (sourceWorkspaceId, or workspaceId on tools that have it).

sourceWorkspaceId.description: The workspace that holds the file, from tarkle_list_workspaces. Send it with fileId.

tools.name: tarkle_list_webhooks
tools.description: List the workspace's webhook endpoints: host, masked address (host only; the path is hidden), events, on or off (and why it was turned off), last success and failure. Never shows a signing secret. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

tools.name: tarkle_create_webhook
tools.description: Add a webhook endpoint: from then on Tarkle sends the named events for this workspace to the address, signed with a secret. events is required: name each one. Asks for confirmation first: the first call creates nothing; show the user the host and the events, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode from the first answer. The signing secret is NEVER returned by this server. After creating, tell the user to open Settings > API > Webhooks in Tarkle and use "New signing secret" on the endpoint's row menu to see its secret once. If an endpoint with the same address and events already exists, that one is returned and nothing is created. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

url.description: The https address Tarkle sends events to.

events.description: The event names to send, named exactly. Ask the user which events they want.

description.description: A short note about what the endpoint is for. null leaves it empty.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved sending these events to this host.

tools.name: tarkle_update_webhook
tools.description: Change a webhook endpoint's address, events, description or turn it on or off (turning it back on clears its failure count). Send only what changes. Changing the address, the events or on/off asks for confirmation first, because that decides where and what Tarkle sends: the first call changes nothing; show the user the host and events, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode. A description-only change does not ask. events, when sent, are named exactly (no wildcards). The signing secret does not change. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

url.description: The new https address Tarkle sends events to.

events.description: The new list of event names, named exactly. It replaces the current list. Ask the user which events they want.

description.description: A short note about what the endpoint is for. null clears it.

enabled.description: true turns the endpoint on (this clears its failure count), false turns it off.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved the change.

tools.name: tarkle_delete_webhook
tools.description: Delete a webhook endpoint and its signing secret: the receiver stops getting events and its delivery log goes with it. Asks for confirmation first: the first call deletes nothing; show the user the host and events, then call again with the same inputs and the confirmationCode. To pause instead, use tarkle_update_webhook with enabled false. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

confirmationCode.description: The code from the first answer of this tool for these exact inputs. Send it only after the user approved deleting this endpoint.

tools.name: tarkle_test_webhook
tools.description: Send one webhook.test event to the endpoint now and show whether it was delivered and the receiver's status code. One try, no retries, and it does not change the endpoint's health. Limited to one test per endpoint per minute. The receiver's response body is not shown. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

webhookId.description: The endpoint to test, from tarkle_list_webhooks.

tools.name: tarkle_get_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: The latest deliveries to one endpoint, newest first: event, status (pending, succeeded, failed), attempts, the receiver's status code and a short cleaned error. Kept 7 days. Use it to see why events are not arriving. Webhooks send signed event data from the workspace to an outside address. Only workspace Owners and Admins can manage them.

webhookId.description: The endpoint whose deliveries to list, from tarkle_list_webhooks.

limit.description: How many deliveries to return, newest first. If omitted, 25 are returned.
